scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: host_1_1_1_1 default-gateway configuration
Mechanism: host_1_1_1_1's correct gateway is 10.1.1.1 (switch_dist_1_1's br0
  address). Its default route was repointed to 10.1.1.254 -- in-subnet but
  unassigned -- so ARP for the gateway never resolves and no off-subnet
  packet leaves the host. On-link destinations (10.1.1.1 via the connected
  route) still work, which is why the gateway pings fine. DNS "times out"
  only because the resolver 10.200.0.2 is off-subnet. The network itself is
  healthy: pod 2 reaches everything, and switch_dist_1_1 still advertises
  10.1.1.0/24.
Localization: host_1_1_1_1
Root cause: host_1_1_1_1's default gateway set to 10.1.1.254 instead of
  10.1.1.1
Fix: restore the default route on host_1_1_1_1 --
  `ip route replace default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0`
scenario.fix_spec:
restore host_1_1_1_1's default route --
`ip route replace default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0`

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: host_1_1_1_1’s local IP routing (default gateway configuration).

Mechanism: The host can reach its local subnet and ARP for 10.1.1.1 (its subnet gateway IP on the L3 switch), so pings to 10.1.1.1 succeed. All off-subnet traffic, however, is sent to the default gateway. Because the default gateway is misconfigured to a nonexistent next-hop (10.1.1.254), ARP resolution for that address fails and the kernel generates “Destination Host Unreachable” locally, causing failures to all remote networks and DNS timeouts.

Localization and evidence:
- On host_1_1_1_1, ip route shows “default via 10.1.1.254 dev eth0” and 10.1.1.0/24 on-link (get_host_net_config).
- Pinging the real gateway 10.1.1.1 succeeds (0% loss), confirming L2/L3 to the SVI on switch_dist_1_1 is fine.
- Pinging the configured default gateway 10.1.1.254 fails with local “Destination Host Unreachable,” and ip neigh shows “10.1.1.254 dev eth0 FAILED,” proving the next-hop does not exist.
- The L3 switch for that subnet (switch_dist_1_1) is correctly addressed at 10.1.1.1 and has OSPF routes to other networks, so upstream routing is healthy.

Root cause: host_1_1_1_1 has an incorrect default gateway set to 10.1.1.254 instead of 10.1.1.1.

Corrective fix: On host_1_1_1_1, replace the default route:
- ip route del default
- ip route add default via 10.1.1.1
Also correct the persistent network config (e.g., /etc/network/interfaces or netplan) to set gateway 10.1.1.1. After this change, off-subnet reachability and DNS queries to 10.200.0.2 will work normally.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names host_1_1_1_1 and attributes the problem to its local default-gateway configuration on the host.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states the default route on host_1_1_1_1 points to 10.1.1.254 instead of the correct 10.1.1.1 and provides supporting evidence.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-network: notes switch_dist_1_1 and the OSPF core are healthy (pod 2 works, the real gateway answers), so no network device needs fixing
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states switch_dist_1_1 (10.1.1.1) responds and has OSPF routes—indicating the distribution switch and core are healthy and do not require fixes.
Replaces the incorrect default route with a route via 10.1.1.1 and advises updating the persistent network configuration, matching the expected fix.
